rules.description: Review repeated owned materialization or preprocessing of invariant input in an established high-volume or hot loop. Fail only when the primary source establishes actual standard-library operations, a significant workload or explicit project performance requirement, unchanged input across iterations, and a visible consumer that can reuse the result without changing semantics. Identify the loop, preprocessing, invariant input, consumer and reusable-result path; explain why hoisting preserves the documented contract, including empty-input and error behavior. Examples include parsing invariant configuration into a Vec or repeatedly collecting and sorting a lookup table for read-only queries. Do not diagnose clone, allocation or collect by spelling alone or duplicate a simple redundant_clone finding. Pass when the workload/performance requirement is not established, preprocessing is already reused, or a listed exception applies. Do not redesign public APIs merely to expose speculative intermediate results.
exceptions: Per-iteration inputs change or the contract requires a fresh independent snapshot, and the visible operations implement that requirement.
Every iteration must transfer a separate owned result to an API/task/retaining consumer; sharing or borrowing would violate the visible ownership or lifetime requirement.

Cheap Arc/Rc sharing, intentional capacity reuse, avoiding worse lock retention/lifetime coupling, documented optimizer elimination or measured workload tradeoffs establish that the current work is appropriate.
Small cold-path work, bounded intentional reservation or no demonstrated caller need does not justify a performance finding.

rules.description: Consider buffering or batching repeated tiny external writes only for an established throughput-oriented high-volume workload. Fail when the primary source establishes the actual unbuffered external sink, repeated tiny standard-library Write operations, and a documented throughput/completion contract without an immediate-delivery requirement or a visible buffering layer. Identify the sink, loop, write sizes and workload; recommend bounded buffering or batching with completion errors observed at the required boundary. A method named write_all alone does not establish its sink or lack of buffering. Pass when the throughput/workload contract is not established, no relevant repeated-write path exists, or a listed exception applies. Do not require whole-file materialization, invent memory ceilings, describe flush as file durability, or add a separate missing-flush finding under this performance rule.
exceptions: A visible std::io::BufWriter or other established buffering/batching layer already coalesces the tiny writes and completion is handled according to the contract.
An interactive protocol requires each small message to reach the peer before waiting for the corresponding response; delaying until a later batch would violate that requirement.
Few or large writes, in-memory Vec targets, bounded streaming requirements, or measured performance establish that further buffering is inappropriate.
